title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Parent registration data including government ID, password, and personal information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.

title: Identification of Parent User
description: Government ID and name data could be used to identify the parent user, potentially leading to unwanted tracking or profiling.

title: Data Manipulation of Registration Information
description: Registration data could be altered or tampered with during processing, potentially leading to incorrect user profiles or authentication issues.

title: Usurpation of Parent Identity
description: With government ID and password, an attacker could potentially impersonate the parent user and gain unauthorized access to the system.

title: Linkability of Registration Data
description: Registration data could be linked to other data sources, enabling correlation of parent user activities across different systems.

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Collection and processing of government ID and sensitive personal data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations like GDPR or CCPA.

title: Parent account data contains personally identifiable information
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account information that includes PII such as names, email addresses, and potentially other identifiers that could directly identify individuals.

title: Unauthorized access to MongoDB users collection
description: If MongoDB is not properly secured with appropriate access controls, unauthorized parties could gain access to the parent account data stored in the collection.

title: Parent account data could be tampered with
description: Without proper access controls and integrity checks, malicious actors could modify the parent account data in MongoDB, leading to data corruption or manipulation.

title: Parent account data could be linked to other data sources
description: The parent account information stored in MongoDB could potentially be linked with other data flows or systems, creating a comprehensive profile of users.

title: Authentication credentials could be compromised
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak or credentials are stolen, attackers could impersonate legitimate users and access their parent account data.

title: User Identifiability via JWT and User Data
description: The JWT token and associated user data transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User can directly identify the individual, potentially exposing personally identifiable information (PII) to unauthorized parties if intercepted or mishandled.

title: Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: User data and JWT tokens sent from the Authentication Service to the Parent User may be exposed during transmission if not properly encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

title: JWT Token Usurpation and Impersonation
description: JWT tokens transmitted to the Parent User could be stolen or intercepted, allowing an attacker to impersonate the authenticated user and gain unauthorized access to protected resources.

title: Excessive Data Minimization Violation
description: The flow transmits 'JWT + user data' which may include more information than necessary for the Parent User's legitimate access needs, violating data minimization principles.

title: Linkability of Child Login to Parent Identity
description: The child's login activity using parent credentials creates a link between the child's digital footprint and the parent's identity, potentially enabling correlation of child activities with parent data across systems.
assumptions: Parent email is used as identifier and parent data exists in other systems

title: Identification of Parent-Child Relationship
description: The parent email and password used for child login can identify both the parent and the child's relationship, potentially revealing family structure and parental involvement in child's digital activities.
assumptions: Parent email is unique identifier and login records are accessible

title: Disclosure of Credentials in Transit
description: Parent email and password transmitted to authentication service could be intercepted during transmission, exposing sensitive authentication credentials to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Transmission channel may not be fully encrypted or credentials could be logged

title: Excessive Data Collection for Child Authentication
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login may exceed data minimization principles, as child-specific credentials could be used instead, collecting more personal data than necessary.
assumptions: Child-specific authentication is not implemented or available

title: Credential Compromise and Unauthorized Access
description: Authentication service could be vulnerable to credential theft, allowing unauthorized parties to impersonate either the child or parent, gaining access to child's account and associated data.
assumptions: Authentication service has vulnerabilities or credentials are stored insecurely

title: Child User Identifiability via JWT and Profiles
description: The JWT token and child profiles transmitted from the Authentication Service contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify the child user across systems and contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens and child profiles contain unique identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be linked to the child user.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profiles may contain sensitive personal information (e.g., health data, location, family information) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the JWT is compromised or intercepted during transmission.
assumptions: Child profiles contain sensitive PII; JWT tokens can be intercepted or stolen.

title: JWT Token Theft and User Impersonation
description: JWT tokens transmitted from the Authentication Service could be stolen or intercepted, allowing an attacker to impersonate the child user and access their profile data or perform actions on their behalf.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted over networks where interception is possible; tokens may not have adequate expiration or revocation mechanisms.

title: Excessive Data Collection in Child Profiles
description: Child profiles may contain more personal data than necessary for the authentication service's purpose, violating data minimization principles and increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Child profiles include fields not strictly required for authentication or service delivery.

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Handling child data (userType child) may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws if appropriate consent, parental controls, or data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: The system handles data of children under applicable age thresholds; regulatory requirements exist for child data processing.

title: Linkability of Government ID to Other Data Sources
description: The child's government ID stored in the profile could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical records) to create a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended scope.

title: Direct Identification of Child Through Profile Data
description: The combination of name, DOB, gender, and government ID in the child profile enables direct identification of the child, which could be misused for tracking or surveillance purposes.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Government ID
description: Government ID information stored in the child profile could be accessed or disclosed to unauthorized parties, leading to identity theft or fraud risks.

title: Tampering with Child Profile Data
description: The child profile data could be altered or corrupted by unauthorized actors, leading to incorrect information being used for identification or access purposes.

title: Parent Impersonation During Profile Creation
description: A malicious actor could impersonate the parent (EE1) to create a false child profile, potentially leading to identity fraud or unauthorized access to child-related services.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Child Data Protection Laws
description: The child profile management process may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection, storage, and processing of children's personal data.

title: Child Profile Data Identifiability
description: Child profile data contains personally identifiable information (PII) that can be used to identify specific children, including names, dates of birth, and contact information.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented, leading to privacy violations.

title: Malicious Modification of Child Profile Data
description: During the store/update process, child profile data could be corrupted or maliciously altered by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate or harmful information.

title: Linkability of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical data) to create comprehensive profiles of children, increasing privacy risks.

title: Unauthorized Profile Updates via Impersonation
description: Unauthorized users could impersonate parents or guardians to update child profile information, potentially leading to identity theft or harmful changes.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: Storing and processing child profile data may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child data protection laws if proper safeguards are not in place.

title: Linkability of Video Search and Engagement Activities
description: Child User's video search history, likes, and comments can be linked across sessions and contexts, potentially revealing patterns of interest and behavior that could be correlated with other data sources.
assumptions: User activities are logged and stored in a way that allows cross-session correlation.

title: Identification Through Behavioral Patterns
description: Video search patterns, comment content, and like behavior could be used to identify the Child User's identity, preferences, or affiliations, especially if combined with other data.
assumptions: Behavioral data is sufficient for identification when combined with other information.

title: Disclosure of Video Content and User Engagement Data
description: Video content accessed through search, along with user comments and likes, could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Video content and engagement data are stored and transmitted without adequate protection.

title: Excessive Collection of Video Search and Engagement Data
description: The Video Management Service may collect more data than necessary, including detailed search history, comment content, and like patterns, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The service collects and retains comprehensive user activity logs beyond what is needed for core functionality.

title: Usurpation of User Account for Posting Comments and Likes
description: If a Child User's account is compromised, an attacker could post comments, like videos, or search on their behalf, leading to unauthorized representation and potential reputation damage.
assumptions: User authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust to prevent account takeover.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Processing of video search, comment, and like data may violate GDPR or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data retention, and user rights to access or delete personal data.
assumptions: The service does not have adequate mechanisms for consent management, data portability, and user data deletion.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Files
description: MongoDB videos collection may be accessible to unauthorized users or systems, leading to exposure of video content and metadata.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed.

title: Linkability of Video Metadata to Individuals
description: Video metadata (timestamps, locations, user IDs) could be linked to identify specific individuals or activities.
assumptions: Metadata contains sufficient identifying information.

title: Identification of Individuals in Video Content
description: Video files may contain visual or audio content that identifies individuals, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Videos capture identifiable people or activities.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data leaks.
assumptions: Metadata is not adequately protected or encrypted.

title: Usurpation of User Identity for Video Upload
description: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate user to upload videos, potentially spreading malicious or unauthorized content.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or bypassed.

title: Child Identity Identification from Search/Watch History
description: Search and watch history stored in child profiles can reveal the child's identity, interests, preferences, and potentially their location or routine patterns, enabling identification of the child even without explicit PII.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, leading to exposure of sensitive behavioral data about the child.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data including search and watch history could be altered by unauthorized actors if proper access controls and audit mechanisms are not implemented.

title: MongoDB DataStore Inadequate Access Controls
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may lack proper encryption, authentication, or authorization mechanisms, increasing risk of data breach and unauthorized access to child behavioral data.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Storage
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate child privacy regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other applicable laws requiring special protections for minors' personal data.

title: Video content reveals personally identifiable information
description: Uploaded videos may contain faces, locations, or other PII that can identify the user or third parties without consent

title: Video data linked across systems and time
description: Videos uploaded by the user can be linked to their identity across different platforms or time periods, creating a comprehensive profile

title: Unauthorized access to video data during approval process
description: Video files may be accessed by unauthorized personnel during the approval/rejection workflow, potentially exposing sensitive content

title: Video data integrity compromised during storage
description: Videos could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during upload, storage, or processing by the Video Management Service

title: Unauthorized video upload by third party
description: Another party could upload videos on behalf of the user without authorization, potentially impersonating the user's intent

title: Child identification from video stream
description: The video stream may contain identifiable information about the child, including facial features, voice, or other biometric data that could be used to identify the child.

title: Unauthorized access to video stream
description: The video stream could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's activities or location.

title: Linking video data to child identity
description: Video data from the stream could be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or other identifiers, creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Child impersonation in video access
description: An unauthorized party could potentially impersonate the child to access or receive the video stream, bypassing authentication controls.

title: Excessive video data collection
description: The video stream may capture more visual or audio data than necessary for the intended purpose, potentially including sensitive information about the child's environment or activities.

title: Child browsing data linkability to identity
description: Child profile browsing data stored in MongoDB collection could be linked to the child's identity through associated metadata, user accounts, or device identifiers, creating a privacy risk for minors.
assumptions: Data contains or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Child identifiability from browsing patterns
description: Browsing behavior data from child profiles could be used to identify specific children through unique browsing patterns, timestamps, or content preferences, violating child privacy expectations.
assumptions: Browsing data contains unique identifiers or patterns

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child browsing data
description: Child browsing data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper data sharing with the AI engine or third parties.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data protection measures

title: AI manipulation of child data and recommendations
description: AI Recommendation Engine could manipulate child browsing data or generate inappropriate recommendations based on sensitive information, potentially exposing children to unsuitable content.
assumptions: AI system has access to raw browsing data without proper safeguards

title: COPPA and child privacy regulation non-compliance
description: Processing child browsing data through AI engine may violate COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) and other child privacy regulations requiring parental consent and data minimization.
assumptions: No parental consent obtained for data processing

title: Linkability of Browsing Data Across Sessions
description: Browsing data sent to third-party advertisers may be linked across different sessions, devices, or platforms, enabling profiling of individual users over time.
assumptions: Advertisers maintain persistent identifiers or use cross-device tracking techniques.

title: Identification of Individuals Through Browsing Patterns
description: Detailed browsing data shared with advertisers could be used to identify specific individuals, revealing personal interests, habits, and potentially sensitive information.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to additional data sources that can be combined with browsing data for identification.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Browsing Data to Third Parties
description: Third-party advertisers may further share or sell the received browsing data to additional entities beyond the original scope, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Advertisers have business incentives to monetize data beyond the intended advertising purpose.

title: Excessive Data Sharing Beyond Advertising Needs
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share more browsing data than necessary for legitimate advertising purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system collects and transmits comprehensive browsing history without proper filtering or anonymization.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Third-Party Data Sharing
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data transfer, and user rights.
assumptions: Proper consent mechanisms and data transfer agreements are not in place or are insufficient.

title: Direct Identification via Government ID Images
description: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information that directly identifies individuals, enabling identification attacks where the stored images can be used to identify data subjects without additional context.
assumptions: ID images are stored in an accessible format and contain sufficient identifying information

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of ID Images
description: Stored government ID images in the file system could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, leading to privacy breaches and potential identity theft.
assumptions: File system lacks proper access controls or encryption

title: Data Manipulation of Stored ID Images
description: Stored government ID images could be altered or tampered with by unauthorized actors, compromising the integrity of the authentication process and potentially enabling fraudulent activities.
assumptions: No integrity checks or digital signatures on stored images

title: Identity Usurpation via Stolen ID Images
description: If government ID images are compromised, attackers could use them to impersonate legitimate users, bypass authentication controls and gain unauthorized access to systems.
assumptions: ID images are not adequately protected and could be extracted from the file system

title: Linkability of ID Images to Other Data
description: Stored government ID images can be linked to other datasets (e.g., transaction records, access logs) creating comprehensive profiles of individuals, enabling tracking and surveillance.
assumptions: ID images are stored in a manner that allows correlation with other data sources

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Sensitive Data Storage
description: Storing government ID images may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) if proper safeguards, retention policies, and consent mechanisms are not implemented.
assumptions: Organizational policies do not meet regulatory requirements for biometric/ID data storage

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS Attack
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to read and exfiltrate authentication tokens through malicious scripts.
assumptions: Attacker has access to the browser environment and can inject malicious scripts

title: User Identity Usurpation via Token Theft
description: Stolen JWT tokens can be used by attackers to impersonate legitimate users, gaining unauthorized access to protected resources and performing actions on behalf of the user.
assumptions: Attacker obtains valid JWT token and has access to the authentication service

title: JWT Token Modification via localStorage Manipulation
description: Attackers can modify JWT tokens stored in localStorage, potentially altering claims or creating forged tokens to bypass authentication checks.
assumptions: Attacker has JavaScript execution capability in the browser context

title: User Data Linkability Through Token Correlation
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers and session information that can be correlated with other data sources, enabling profiling and tracking of user activities across services.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that can be correlated with token information

title: User Identifiability Through Token Exposure
description: JWT tokens may contain user identifiers (sub, email, etc.) that can be exposed through localStorage, making users directly identifiable to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: JWT token payload contains identifiable user information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history
description: Child's historical data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches, violating the child's privacy expectations.
assumptions: System has adequate access controls but may have vulnerabilities; parent has legitimate access rights.

title: Excessive data displayed to parent
description: The system may display more child history information than necessary for the parent's review, including sensitive details that could be unnecessary for parental oversight.
assumptions: System may not implement data minimization principles; parent may need only summary information.

title: Child identification through history data
description: Child's historical data may contain personally identifiable information that could identify the child, even when accessed by the parent, potentially revealing sensitive personal details.
assumptions: Child history may include dates, locations, or activities that could identify the child.

title: Linkability of child history to other data
description: Child's history data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, medical data) creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds parental review needs.
assumptions: Data may be accessible across systems; linkage could occur through common identifiers.
